newsitem.title: USA: MCI in large-scale Internet video pact.
newsitem.headline: MCI in large-scale Internet video pact.

text.p: MCI Communications Corp and privately held Progressive Networks Inc said Tuesday they would offer a service to deliver audio and video to broadcast-size audiences over the Internet.

The companies said the new service, known as "RealNetwork," will increase the viability of the Internet as a mass broadcast medium by combining MCI's high-speed Internet backbone network -- one of the world's largest and fastest -- with Progressive Networks' multimedia streaming technology.
Streaming is a compression technology for transmitting large amounts of audio or video data via the Internet.

Walt Disney Co's ABC News; and ESPN, Disney's joint venture with Hearst Corp; Home & Garden Television; Chicago-based JAMtv; and the Seattle Mariners baseball team are among the first content providers to broadcast audio and video on the RealNetwork, the companies said.

MCI and Progressive Networks are launching the RealNetwork as a service for businesses including broadcasters, content providers and large corporations to transmit "live" and "on-demand" programming to large audiences.

They said the service has the potential to reach simultaneous audiences of up to 50,000 and daily audiences of 10 to 15 million visitors through a combination of live and on-demand broadcasts via the Internet and private intranets.
The RealNetwork also can be expanded to serve larger audiences as demand increases, they said.

MCI has made its Internet backbone broadcast-ready by strategically placing Progressive Networks' splitter and multicast technology throughout its IP network, allowing any Internet user to access RealNetwork broadcasts.
This integration greatly expands the number of people who can tune-in to Internet broadcasts while introducing higher levels of audio and video quality over the Net.
As examples of how the system will be used, ABC News has added multimedia capabilities to ABCNews.com to broadcast live news feeds and on-demand reports from ABC News over the Internet.

Atlantic Records will conduct live concerts in its virtual venue, Digital Arena, featuring its label artists. ESPN will use the RealNetwork to broadcast professional basketball games live on ESPN SportsZone, the companies said.
Progressive Networks is based in Seattle, Wash.
